2610.13783.title: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes
2610.13783.paper_summary: Memes play a central role in modern online communication, especially in contexts of political conflict where visual and textual cues combine to convey persuasive messages. We study persuasive technique detection in Ukrainian memes using vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce UkrMeme, a dataset of 200 organically produced Ukrainian wartime memes annotated for persuasion techniques, and PTM-UA, a Ukrainian translation of a subset of the Propaganda 950 benchmark that preserves original visual content while translating meme text. We evaluate VLMs in a zero-shot prompting setup across image, text, and multimodal inputs using hierarchical F1 metrics. Finally, we compare Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) and model-generated token attributions and analyze the semantic categories of evidence emphasized by each explanation method.
2610.13783.paper_summary_zh: 迷因在現代線上溝通中扮演著核心角色，特別是在政治衝突的背景下，視覺和文本提示結合以傳達具說服力的信息。<lb/>我們使用視覺-語言模型（VLMs）研究烏克蘭迷因中的說服技術檢測。<lb/>我們介紹了UkrMeme，一個包含200個有機生成的烏克蘭戰時迷因的數據集，並對其進行了說服技術的標註，還有PTM-UA，這是一個保留原始視覺內容的Propaganda 950基準子集的烏克蘭語翻譯，同時翻譯迷因文本。<lb/>我們在零樣本提示設置下評估VLMs，涵蓋圖像、文本和多模態輸入，並使用層級F1指標。<lb/>最後，我們比較層級相關性傳播（LRP）和模型生成的標記歸因，並分析每種解釋方法所強調的證據的語義類別。
